DC95: Scroll level and shift all objects down
Used by the routine at DE91.
Advances the level scroll one step, then shifts every object in the $5B11 table down by one row (+$05) until the $90 end marker.

DC98 LD IX,$5B11
DC9C INC (IX+$05) Scroll object down one row

DCA2 ADD IX,DE
DCA4 LD A,(IX+$00) Stop at $90 end marker
DCA7 SUB $90
DCA9 JR NZ,$DC9C
DCAB LD ($FDEE),A
DCAE RET
DCAF: Periodically spawn a new enemy from the edge
Used by the routine at DEEF.
Spawns a new enemy in from the screen edge on a countdown, picking the side and column at random and dropping it into a free slot.
DCAF LD A,($FDFB) Spawning enabled ($FDFB)?
DCB2 OR A
DCB3 RET Z
DCB4 DEC (IY+$7D) Count down the spawn timer
DCB7 RET NZ
DCB8 LD ($FDFD),A

DCD4 LD C,$0C
DCD6 CALL $E10F Find free enemy slot in $5B11 table, inside $E01B
DCD9 RET Z
DCDA SET 6,(IX+$0B) Mark new enemy (flag bit 6)
DCDE RET
DCDF: Initialization and go to game main loop
Used by the routine at DC89.
Sets up a fresh game: clears the object table, places the player at the starting position, resets the projectile tables and seeds the random state, then drops into the main loop.

DD1C XOR $AA Second byte is the first flipped

DD1F INC L

DD8D: Draw object IX: select sprite frame, clip, blit
Used by the routine at DD71.
Input
IX Address of the 20-byte object record
Draws one object and works out its clipping. It picks the sprite frame from the object's state and direction, checks the row against the visible band, and on success paints a shadow strip and draws the sprite; an object outside the band is skipped or has its draw flag cleared.

DD98 JR NC,$DDA2

DDE0 CP $5F
DDE2 JR NC,$DE0B
DDE4 LD C,$5F

DDE9 JR Z,$DE2A

DDFC INC L

DDFF INC H
DE00 DEC L
DE01 LD BC,$0555
DE04 LD (HL),C ...and the row below
DE05 DEC L
DE06 DJNZ $DE04
DE08 POP BC
DE09 JR $DE2A
DE0B RES 5,(IX+$0B) Off screen: clear the draw flag

DE39 CP C
DE3A JP P,$DE52

DE45 JR Z,$DE4D
DE47 LD A,(IX+$04)
DE4A CP $1F
DE4C RET NC

DE52 LD A,(IX+$05) Special mid-screen row band
DE55 CP $E0
DE57 JR NC,$DE3D
DE59 CP $40

DE91: Game's main loop, Part 1
Used by the routines at DCDF and DEEF.
First half of the frame. It kills the player if their alive flag has gone, waits for the interrupt marking the frame boundary, then scrolls the level and redraws every object before dropping into Part 2.

E0BF: Map-scan tails: step to the next row, or set the Area flag and return
A run of short tails for the map scan in E01B: each steps down a row and rejoins the scan, stores the new row, or raises the Area-complete flag when the player is at the end row with Up held. Only $E0D8 has a discovered caller, so the entry points of the other tails are not yet traced, and a few bytes between them (at $E0CA, $E0EF, $E0F5 and $E0FC) do not decode into anything sensible -- they may be reached at a different alignment.

FD91: Interrupt return trampoline, built in RAM
Used by the routine at 7357.
A three-byte JP built in RAM and used as the interrupt handler's way back. The opcode byte is installed at startup from $7A42 and the target is rewritten on every interrupt by $735E with the address that was interrupted, so 7357 finishes by jumping through here. These bytes are dual-use: they sit in the variable area yet are executed as code.
